sources.entry: Fusio - API management platform which helps to build and manage REST APIs. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: Fusio is a self-hosted, open-source PHP API management platform and API gateway that turns backend logic and databases into REST API products, with MCP support for AI agents.
summary.what_it_does: Fusio exposes SQL/NoSQL databases as REST APIs, routes and load-balances traffic between microservices, and lets you write reusable API actions in PHP or JavaScript (with Worker actions for building logic in the backend). Actions are bound to HTTP operations and can be configured through generated backend forms. An AI Agent feature can generate worker action logic from natural-language prompts using providers the README names (Ollama, ChatGPT, Gemini). The README also describes a self-service developer portal, SDK generation for several languages, subscription plans and quotas, and real-time usage analytics. Installation is via Docker (with MySQL) or manually with PHP, supporting MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite, plus a web installer.
use_cases: expose a legacy database as a REST API
route and orchestrate traffic between microservices
manage and publish a public API with a developer portal
generate client SDKs for API consumers
turn backend logic into tools for AI agents
monetize an API with plans and quotas
how_to_run: docker compose up -d (using the fusio/fusio image with a MySQL service, as shown in the README)
git clone the repository and configure APP_CONNECTION in .env
notable: Database API gateway that exposes existing SQL/NoSQL databases as REST endpoints
Native Model Context Protocol (MCP) support to expose APIs as tools for AI agents
Worker actions let you write logic in JavaScript or Python in the backend, plus PHP actions
Built-in marketplace for sharing apps and actions, with an optional ecosystem of companion services (SDKgen, TypeHub, APIgen, APImon)
caveats: The development server (php -S) is for testing only; production needs Nginx/Apache or Docker, per the README
Several ecosystem services (Marketplace, SDKgen, TypeHub, APIgen, APImon) require separate registration or credentials and are described as separate services
Marketplace and SDK generation features need client credentials configured in System / Config
